enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1041 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1040 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

 - Breezy winds expected ahead of a Pacific cold front on
   Saturday. West winds will gust 35 to 40 mph in the afternoon,
   and up to 45 mph along east facing slopes and exposed
   ridgelines.

 - Cooler temperatures and fair weather are expected for most of 
   next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 944 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

The closed low over the Great Basin yesterday has weakened into an
open trough extending across Utah into southern Nevada. This
system will move across northern Arizona tonight into tomorrow
morning, then across New Mexico through the day tomorrow
(Saturday). 

A few spotty showers will graze the northern Gila Region in the 
morning, and some sprinkles could reach northern Grant County, but
mostly we'll just see some uptick in cloud cover and breezy west-
southwest winds. By afternoon, gusts 35 to 40 mph will be common,
with a few gusts around 45 mph possible along east-facing mountain
slopes and exposed higher elevation ridgelines. No dust is
expected.

High pressure will build in Saturday night, then the race will be
on to see if winds can diminish fast enough to maximize
radiational cooling. Dewpoints dropping into the upper-10s to
lower-20s and a lack of cloud cover will help. Weakest gradient
will be north of the I-10 corridor in New Mexico. Upper-10s in the
Gila cold spots are likely. Jornada Range and the Hatch Valley
look like a fair bet for reaching the freezing mark. The Mesilla
Valley is a 50/50 toss-up. We'll get another chance Sunday
night/Monday morning as winds will be lighter. 

After notching a high 10 degrees above normal at ELP today
(Friday, and 75 degrees), temperatures will drop Saturday and
Sunday with highs Sunday topping out near 60 over much of the
lowlands, about 3 to 5 degrees below normal.

Another weak trough will sweep through on Monday, with little wind
and very low precip chances. Models still having a tough time with
the pattern across the CONUS late week, but benign weather is most
favored.

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 944 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

VFR conditions and light winds through the overnight. An
approaching upper level disturbance and Pacific cold front will 
bring increasing WSW winds on Saturday. Model soundings suggest
some SCT-BKN clouds around 5000-7000 feet are possible just ahead
of the front, though precip chances look nil. Expect a few gusts
around 30 to 35 knots after 19Z. Winds will shift to the NW and
diminish quickly after sunset.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1052 AM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

Breezy to windy conditions are expected this afternoon and again
Saturday as an upper level trough moves across the Rockies. While
the winds will be near critical speeds, RH's will remain in the
20-35% range for much of the lowlands and even higher in area
mountains. Temperatures will cool down by Saturday to near normal
and remain there into early next week with winds also on the
decrease. Vent rates will be very good Saturday but drop down to
poor to fair for Sunday as winds die off and mixing heights drop. 

&&
